Snow Event Profile Maker 3.5.0

12600 lines of code

Powered by real NOAA RSI methodology with location-based impact scaling

Storm Name

Input Mode

Snow War Tiers

All — snow war activity tiers, ordered by the packable snow depth that reaches them — from a single disputed flake up past 30,000″. Every city in a storm lands on exactly one of these, based on how much of its precipitation packs.

Add Cities — Heat Index

Great Lakes water temps (°F) Optional. A cool lake cuts lakeshore highs (lake breeze); a warm lake adds humidity and keeps nights warm. Every Michigan city is affected.

Water War Tiers

All — water war tiers, ordered by the heat that reaches them — from a condensation ring on a glass to the first rain of the next universe. Heat alone decides the tier: the heat score through the realistic range, the deadliest wet-bulb readings at the top of Continental, and air temperature alone past 134°F.

Cozy War Tiers

All — cozy war tiers, ordered by the effective rain that reaches them — from a dry day that sends everyone outside to rain beyond anything on record. Every town that gets rain lands on exactly one of these; wind and low pressure push it higher.

Fill In The Gaps — Heat

Estimate any city not in the run. The simulator carries over how far above normal the heat is — not the raw temperature — weighted toward the nearest entered cities, and fades it out beyond 500 miles. Past 1,200 miles a city is outside the heat event.

Add Cities — Severe Storm

Replay Historic Storm

Type the name of any storm from the Historic Reference list and we'll generate a matching profile — template picked from the storm's named region, severity picked from its RSI. Output renders exactly like the other modes.

Closest Historic Comparison — Storm Reference

Every storm used as a "Closest Historic Comparison" benchmark, sorted lowest to highest RSI. The simulator picks whichever of these is nearest to your generated storm's RSI score.

Describe the Storm

Mention cities, regions, storm types, severity, snow amounts — whatever feels natural.

Add Cities

Search 500+ cities worldwide — population, region, and snow resilience included

How far the storm reaches beyond the entered cities. Nor'easters and lake-effect bands are tight (Minimal/Low); continental outbreaks are broad (Wide/Extreme).

Fill In The Gaps

Enter any city not already in the storm and we'll estimate how much snow it would get — interpolated from the entered cities using inverse-distance weighting, with distance falloff and climate dampening for cities far outside the storm's reach.
